#644 — THE declaration of the tool links both terminals ship, and the engine that materialises, verifies, repairs and rolls them back. It exists because #638 (/usr/bin/env absent), #640 (the same absence killing every `#!/usr/bin/env` shebang) and #641 (a login shell pointing at a binary the zip did not carry) were three instances of ONE defect: a link between the fixed filesystem and the package layer was written once, by hand, at bake time, and nothing on the phone could tell that it had gone dangling. Each was fixed individually. This block stops that class instead: the links are DATA, and cloud-store is a generic loop over that data.

TWO terminals, both stay (ac_cloud-termux is Termux, ac_cloud-nix-on-droid is Nix-on-Droid; they are not the same app and do not merge). They share this file, the engine, and the login wiring; they differ only in the two values below that say where a tool's real binary lives and whether a package manager exists to update it.

NOT a reimplementation of nix. Nix already has generations, an atomic switch and rollback for a PACKAGE SET, and the nix terminal drives exactly that (package_manager: nix → `nix profile upgrade` / `nix-env --rollback` against nix_profile). What nix does NOT manage, and what the three defects above all lived in, is the $HOME-side link tree pointing INTO whichever package layer the terminal has — a tree the termux terminal has no nix for at all. That tree is what this engine owns, with nix's semantics (generations, one-symlink atomic switch, rollback) because those are the right semantics, not because nix is being copied.
_comment_adding_a_tool: DATA ONLY, no code change, and that is the whole point of #644. A tool enters the store when it appears in the list `terminals.<t>.tools` points at — ac_cloud-nix-on-droid/build.json::forks.nixdroid.bootstrap.default_packages.binaries (alongside its attr and provides entry) or ac_cloud-termux/rootfs/rootfs.json::binaries. render-store.py re-renders declaration.sh from that list at build time and the engine loops over it at runtime. Nothing here, and nothing in cloud-store, names a tool.

toolset._doc: #737 -- THE tool set both terminals ship baked in, working at the first prompt with no install step. ONE list, consumed by both bakes: render-store.py::tools_of prepends it to each terminal's own list, so it reaches the termux rootfs build (resolve.py merges it into the roster install-in-rootfs.sh installs and command -v's, and verify-inside.sh executes under the shipped proot) and the nix bake (bake_default_packages.py fails when the realized profile lacks bin/<name>; verify_login_closure.py fails when the shipped zip does not resolve /<profile>/bin/<name> to a chmod-ed file). Packaging stays per terminal: termux installs these through apt, tarballs and npm (rootfs.json + the fleet tool belt), nix through attrs (build.json default_packages.attrs/provides). Neither app's own list may repeat a name from here -- both renderers refuse it -- so this cannot quietly become two lists again. `which` is here because the on-device checklist runs `which`, and nothing else on the nix side provides it. python3 is deliberately NOT here: #665 measured it as 19% of the nix OS image with nothing asking for it; the termux terminal keeps it as its own extra because hermes runs in a venv there.
toolset._doc_flock_cmp: linux-store (linux_tools below) refuses to start without flock (its one-mutating-run lock) and cmp (its re-exec and store-object comparisons); jq it already had here. Both are Debian base-image binaries (util-linux, diffutils), so the termux tree gains nothing but a declaration; the nix profile gets util-linuxMinimal and diffutils (build.json default_packages.attrs/provides).

linux_tools._doc: THE declaration of what both terminals ship from cloud-u-linux: the `linux-store` and `linux-account` CLIs and the fish greeting. ONE pin, declared like rootfs.json::shared_toolbelt: the two repositories are separate git histories, so a file cannot be shared by path; both are public, so the bakes read each file at this exact commit from raw.githubusercontent.com. `ref` is the content address: bumping it (and the per-file sha256 beside it) is an edit to THIS file, which is an identity file of both rootfs artifacts, so a CLI or greeting change republishes both terminals instead of hiding outside the gate. fetch-linux-tools.py is the only fetcher; it refuses any byte that differs from `sha256` (the same discipline as fetch-proot.py), and both bakes install exactly what it plans: ac_cloud-termux/rootfs/build-rootfs.sh into the tree, ac_cloud-nix-on-droid bake_default_packages.py into the bootstrap zip. The install paths are the same absolute paths in both images, and login-init.sh makes sure /usr/local/bin is on PATH and /usr/share is a fish data dir, so neither terminal needs a different wiring. terminal-parity-guard.py fails when one terminal stops installing or verifying any entry below.

licence._doc: Checked at the pin: the repository root carries LICENSE (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, `Required Notice: Copyright 2026 Diego Nepomuceno Marcos`) and LICENSING.md says all original code in it is the licensor's own with no third-party carve-outs; da_dtk/ repeats the same LICENSE. These files are therefore the owner's own work, not a third party's, and are redistributed here by the copyright holder; they travel as separate files inside the rootfs artifacts (aggregation), never compiled into the GPL-3.0-only terminal apps. licenses/inventory.json lists each as a `fetched:` subject.
licence.notice: Required Notice: Copyright 2026 Diego Nepomuceno Marcos — https://diegonmarcos.com

linux_tools._doc_needs: Runtime dependencies of the CLIs (linux-store: jq sha256sum flock find mv readlink cmp, sops and an age key for its secret layer; linux-account: jq sha256sum). Every name must be in toolset.binaries above, so both terminals' existing bake gates prove it is installed; the guard refuses a name that is not. The TUI scripts (linux-store-tui.py, linux-account-tui.py) are deliberately not shipped: both CLIs fall back to their sh screens without them, and the nix image has no python3 (#665).

startup._doc: The steps a terminal runs when it starts or is baked, declared once so the two cannot drift. Every `startup-step: <id>` marker comment in the files listed under terminals.<t>.startup_files is one step; terminal-parity-guard.py requires the SAME set in both terminals and every id below to be implemented in each (shared ids live in login-init.sh, which both terminals source). A step added to one terminal without the other, or lost from one, is red.

steps.wipe_stale_root: clear the previous root / staging read-only-safely before a re-extract; quiet, one summary line, never fatal (termux enter.sh wipe_rootfs; nix BootstrapStaging.wipeQuiet)
steps.rish_bridge: bind the rish launcher into the root
steps.dns_resolver: lookups go to the app's DNS bridge
steps.linux_tools_install: bake the pinned linux-store, linux-account and fish_greeting into the image (fetch-linux-tools.py)
steps.agent_auth_env: agent CLI credentials from the app's env file
steps.linux_path: /usr/local/bin on PATH, where the baked CLIs live
steps.fish_greeting_path: /usr/share a fish data dir, where the baked greeting lives
steps.linux_first_start: first start: linux-store switch when its prerequisites exist, else one line saying what is missing

store._doc: Runtime layout, under $HOME so it survives every rootfs/bootstrap update (termux binds $HOME as /root; the nix terminal's $HOME is the real app-private path). `current` is the ONE symlink an apply flips, with a single rename(2) — a half-switched profile is therefore not a reachable state. generations/ keeps the previous ones so rollback is a switch, not a rebuild.
store._doc_install_dir: Where the engine, its rendered declaration and the login wiring are SHIPPED (read-only), as opposed to store.root where the store is BUILT (writable, in $HOME). Relative like every other baked path: the nix terminal extracts it under $PREFIX and bin/login binds $PREFIX/usr onto /usr; the termux terminal binds the same-named APK asset directory onto /usr/lib/cloud-store inside proot. Both therefore resolve it at /usr/lib/cloud-store, which is the one literal login-init.sh carries — render-store.py hard-fails if that literal and this value ever disagree.
store._doc_engine_in_home: `cloud-store` is also copied INTO the store ($HOME/.cloud-store/cloud-store) and linked into its own bin/, so the engine that manages the links is itself a declared link and is on PATH from $HOME, editable in place. Diego asked for the shell engine in the home directory; this is that, without giving up a read-only shipped copy to repair from.

agent_auth._doc: #790 where a login finds the agent CLIs' credentials. Both terminals keep them in their libs:core fleet-config.json store `agent-auth` (class secret), which Configs ▸ Account imports from the declared profile over the #783 FleetConfig contract -- so a fresh install, a re-unpack or a new phone is logged in without /login. The app (AgentAuth.java in each terminal) writes that store, on every start, to THIS file under $HOME, mode 0600 in a 0700 dir, one `export NAME='value'` per key (the store's keys ARE the variable names: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for claude, OPENROUTER_API_KEY for goose and hermes), and deletes it when the store is empty. login-init.sh sources it, so every session -- typed, RUN_COMMAND or /api/terminal/exec -- starts with them in its environment, and no secret sits in a file the user edits, in the rootfs, or in a log. Relative to $HOME, which both terminals keep outside the tree an update replaces (termux binds it as /root).

nix._doc: ac_cloud-nix-on-droid. The package layer IS a nix profile, so targets are a fixed prefix under it (never a /nix/store hash: every hash moves with the nixpkgs pin, which is how a literal rots into a dangling link silently) and updates/package-generation rollback are delegated to nix itself.

linux_tools._doc: Where this terminal installs and proves the linux_tools entries: the bake that writes them into the image, and the files whose checks name every entry (the guard requires each cli and the greeting in all of them).

fixed_links._doc: #640's link, now VERIFIED and REPAIRABLE rather than only written once. bake_default_packages.py still emits the SYMLINKS.txt line — it has to, nothing has logged in yet at extraction time — but until #644 nothing could notice afterwards that it had gone missing, and its absence is precisely what made every `#!/usr/bin/env` shebang fail. It is a fixed absolute path rather than a store link because the kernel resolves a shebang against /usr/bin/env and nothing else.

termux._doc: ac_cloud-termux. A baked Debian glibc tree entered through proot: no nix, so the generation/atomic-switch/rollback machinery here is the real implementation rather than a delegation. Targets are searched along the standard FHS path because rootfs.json installs them through apt, tarballs, npm and pip venvs, each into its own dir (install-in-rootfs.sh symlinks venv console scripts into /usr/local/bin), and the declaration should not have to restate which mechanism produced which tool.

linux_tools._doc: Where this terminal installs and proves the linux_tools entries: the bake that writes them into the image, and the files whose checks name every entry (the guard requires each cli and the greeting in all of them).

termux._doc_package_manager: Honest `none`: the tool set is baked at build time from rootfs.json and a phone cannot add to it, so `cloud-store update` says so instead of pretending. The store is still worth having here — the rootfs tree is REPLACED on every update while $HOME persists, so links from $HOME into it are exactly what goes stale.
